**Isoloop 0.1.0 is the first release of event-loop isolation for JavaScript apps.** Build your app from parts that run apart and work together: when one blocks or crashes on its own worker, the others keep working, and it restarts and catches up from the bus.

## What you get

- **Failures stay contained.** By default each part is an isolate with its own event loop and heap. A slow widget, a runaway engine or a crash doesn't freeze the rest of your app.
- **Recovery is built in.** The supervisor notices a blocked or crashed isolate, restarts it, and shows a fallback with Retry if it has to give up. The restarted isolate reads what it needs back from the bus.
- **One typed way to share data.** Topics with schemas checked on every publish, per-isolate grants, retention, replay, backpressure, and request and reply.
- **History that lasts.** Mark a topic persistent and its records and committed positions survive a reload and a restart of the bus.
- **Placement is a switch.** Give an isolate its own worker, or name a pool to save memory and start-up time. Its code stays the same.
- **The UI you already write.** React 18 and 19, Preact 10 and 11, plain DOM, canvas in the isolate's own worker, or no UI at all.
- **The tools around it.** A Vite plugin, test helpers for isolates and contracts, JSON Schema export of your contracts, and a devtools panel that shows isolates, topics and live records.
- **Ready for coding agents.** A "build with Isoloop" skill, a dev MCP that lets an agent inspect your running app, and your own topics offered to agents as tools.

See it run: [the live examples](https://isoloop.dev/examples/), from four isolates to a 72-widget dashboard.

## Packages

- **`@isoloop/host`:** the kernel on the page. It starts, places and supervises isolates, and draws their UI.
- **`@isoloop/runtime`:** what an isolate runs on: its lifecycle, the bus client, calls to the page, and test helpers.
- **`@isoloop/bus`:** topics and contracts, schema checks, retention, replay, persistence, and test helpers for contracts.
- **`@isoloop/vite`:** the Vite plugin: worker URLs, isolate builds and development headers.
- **`@isoloop/react`:** write isolates as React components, with hooks for topics, requests and the page.
- **`@isoloop/preact`:** the same hooks for Preact components.
- **`isoloop`:** the command line: contracts as JSON Schema, the dev MCP server, and the agent skill.
- **`@isoloop/devtools`** (experimental): a panel for isolates, topics and live records, with restart, kill and block.
- **`@isoloop/balancer`** (experimental): places isolates by measured load, moves them and quarantines the ones that block.
- **`@isoloop/webmcp`** (experimental): offers your app's tools to a browser's agent through WebMCP.

## Install

```sh
npm install @isoloop/host @isoloop/runtime @isoloop/bus zod
npm install -D @isoloop/vite
```

Add `@isoloop/react` or `@isoloop/preact` for those frameworks, then follow [Getting started](https://github.com/isoloop/isoloop/blob/v0.1.0/docs/guide/getting-started.md). For agents, with Node 26 or later: `npm install -D isoloop`, then `npx isoloop skill add`.

## Good to know

- **Experimental,** so they may change in any minor: the balancer, devtools and inspection, agent tools and WebMCP, consumer groups, and request and reply.
- **The trade:** isolation costs CPU, memory and start-up time. [What it costs](https://github.com/isoloop/isoloop/blob/v0.1.0/docs/guide/limits.md#what-it-costs) has the measurements.

## Limitations

- **Not a security boundary.** It contains failures, not hostile code.
- **A pool fails together.** Its members share one event loop, so one that blocks restarts them all.
- **No synchronous layout or page DOM.** Measuring, focus and scrolling are async calls, so some UI libraries don't fit in an isolate.
- **Input arrives as a message.** `preventDefault()` in an isolate comes too late, and drag and drop isn't forwarded.
- **No server-side rendering.** An isolate's content appears once its worker has started.
- **Inline styles in your CSP.** A page that shows an isolate's UI needs `style-src 'unsafe-inline'`.
- **Browsers only:** Chrome 108, Firefox 114 and Safari 16.4 or later.

[All the limits](https://github.com/isoloop/isoloop/blob/v0.1.0/docs/guide/limits.md).
